prior_result: PR #3218 found that lambda 0.8 at step_size 0.05 lost against lambda 0 on all three development seed pairs. One trace arm discovered upstream reward early but later preferred the left reward. Discovery alone did not explain the failure.
hypothesis: At fixed lambda 0.8, lowering step_size from 0.05 to 0.014 will improve lifetime mean reward because accumulated eligibility can make the original per-feature learning step too large. The two no-trace arms test whether any benefit is generic step-size sensitivity rather than a lambda-specific interaction.
mechanism_basis: The existing SARSA implementation uses accumulating head eligibility and decays inactive-head traces with gamma * lambda approximately 0.72. A repeatedly activated scalar trace has a geometric accumulation scale approximately 1/(1-0.72). The single prespecified reduced step is 0.05*(1-0.9*0.8)=0.014. This is a heuristic for a mechanism probe, not an optimality or stability guarantee for varying features, shared biases or this control task.
design: Matched 2-by-2 factorial. Only lamda and step_size vary; every direct contrast holds one fixed. Each arm is remeasured on the same three fresh seeds. No prior shard is reused.
seed_role: Fresh development seeds, not previous scorecard or calibration seeds and never scientific held-out evaluation.
primary_contrast: trace_scaled minus trace_original within each seed
primary_decision: Support the bounded trace-step-reduction hypothesis only if all three primary paired differences are strictly positive and their mean exceeds 0.01. Otherwise report negative if the mean is nonpositive, or inconclusive for mixed/nonqualifying positive means. No secondary metric can rescue failure.
interaction_decision: Call the bounded result consistent with a lambda-specific step-size interaction only if the primary rule passes and all three interaction contrasts are strictly positive with mean above 0.01. A primary win without that interaction is only fixed-lambda calibration support. Neither outcome establishes that excessive step size was the sole cause of the old failure.
reference_comparisons: Report trace_scaled minus each of no_trace_original and no_trace_scaled with all per-seed values and spreads; no reference-dev selection or promotion occurs even if positive.
secondary_metrics: first upstream reward event (null is censored)
fixed-checkpoint action values and eligibility norms
fixed_controls: Default six-state RiverSwim, gamma 0.9, epsilon 0.5 to 0.02 over 2500 steps, empty hidden network and shared linear-head biases. Every transition uses the unchanged full ReferenceLifeRunner and exact-dispatch adapter. No forced exploration, reward shaping, horizon change, faster substitute runner or initialization intervention.
resource_policy: At most two independent CPU processes at once in the declared pair schedule; OMP/OpenBLAS/MKL threads 1 and JAX preallocation false. Equal event/update-attempt budgets. Record endpoint numeric state bytes and leaf counts; total process/native peak memory and calibrated timing are unmeasured. Added trace computation is not assumed free. API preflight seed100699 is excluded.
integrity_policy: Commit plan and script and open a draft PR before comparison execution. Record UTC start/end, exact plan/script/source/runtime identities, immutable full raw traces and fixed diagnostics. Stop the schedule on a failed shard without retry or seed substitution; retain its failure prefix if available and logs. Results remain tied to the clean frozen input commit. Do not modify plan, script, parameters, roster, thresholds or horizon after inspecting outcomes.
scope_limit: Permanently nonpromoting development-only causal diagnostic. Three seed pairs and two chosen step sizes cannot establish an optimal step, general superiority, statistical confidence, transfer/retention, frozen-scorecard qualification, reference-dev or scientific evidence. Existing artifacts and frozen gates stay unchanged. Any further tuning requires a different preregistered hypothesis and new seeds.
